Respected Parliament
National Assembly
Twenty-first Session
Complete Minutes
Proceedings
May 13, 2083
Wednesday
Meeting Number -

The meeting of the National Assembly commenced today at 3:16 PM under the chairmanship of the Honorable Chairperson, Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.

Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable members,
The proceedings of the meeting shall commence. I would like to provide time to the Honorable Minister for Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Sovita Gautam, on behalf of the Honorable Prime Minister and Home Minister, Mr. Balendra Shah, to present the proposal for consideration of the "Bill to Amend the Representative Council Member Election Act, 2083" received with a message from the House of Representatives.

Honorable Minister for Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Ms. Sovita Gautam: -
(3:17 PM)
Honorable Chairperson,
With the permission of the Honorable Chairperson, I present before this esteemed assembly the proposal for consideration of the "Bill to Amend the Representative Council Member Election Act, 2083" received with a message from the House of Representatives.
Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable members, the discussion on the proposal presented by the Honorable Minister for Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Ms. Sovita Gautam, on behalf of the Honorable Prime Minister and Home Minister, Mr. Balendra Shah, for consideration of the "Bill to Amend the Representative Council Member Election Act, 2083" received with a message from the House of Representatives, shall now commence.
I inform the honorable members that only the theoretical aspects of the bill and its clauses can be discussed.
I request the honorable members who wish to participate in the discussion to submit their names within two minutes.
I have allocated three minutes to each honorable member participating in the discussion. Honorable member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar.

Honorable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Nepal Communist Party): - Honorable Chairperson,
I am present to express my views on this bill, the "Bill to Amend the Representative Council Member Election Act, 2083," presented by the Honorable Minister on behalf of the Honorable Prime Minister. Regarding this bill, Honorable Chairperson, the election of the members of the House of Representatives was conducted under specific circumstances and in a specific manner. This is because a political change occurred in the country following the movement on Bhadra 23rd, and the government formed at that time conducted the election of the members of the House of Representatives. However, while conducting this election, individuals who were not eligible to vote in the previous election had become eligible by the time of the 2082 Representative Council Member election. Therefore, they should not have been deprived of their right to vote. The then government brought this amendment, the Representative Council Member Election Act, keeping this in mind. In that sense, the government's step was correct because those individuals were not deprived of their voting rights, and subsequently, the election of the House of Representatives was held. However, one thing is that this bill was brought in haste. We did not get enough time to discuss it thoroughly because it was brought in haste. If the bill had been brought with more time, we would have discussed it further, consulted, refined it, and perhaps some omissions would not have occurred. But that could not happen. I wish to draw the government's attention through the Honorable Chairperson that the government should not act in such haste in the future as it did when bringing this bill. Not only regarding this bill, but also regarding many other matters that the government undertakes, I want to state that the government at that time, the government that conducted the election of the House of Representatives, has already been dissolved. A new government has taken its place. I wish to state that this government should learn from the mistakes of the previous government and present all bills or documents and matters that require discussion in the assembly with ample time, providing us with such an opportunity. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable member Padam Bahadur Pariyar.

Honorable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress): - Honorable Chairperson,
We are in the theoretical discussion of the bill to amend the "Representative Council Member Election Act, 2074." Honorable Chairperson, Article 84 of the Constitution of Nepal mandates that the members of the federal parliament, particularly the members of the House of Representatives and the National Assembly, be brought in based on an inclusive and proportional electoral system. Specifically, this bill has been brought forward stating the need for amendment based on the population percentage from the 2078 census. However, Article 84, Sub-section (3) of the Constitution also makes a constitutional provision for ensuring the representation of persons with disabilities. Similarly, the Supreme Court, through an interim order on Poush 18, 2082, has directed the Government of Nepal and the Election Commission to make arrangements for the representation of persons with disabilities. However, as this bill is being presented, only six clusters are included: Dalit, Adivasi Janajati, Khas-Arya, Madhesi, Tharu, and Muslim communities. Specifically, this bill has failed to ensure the representation of persons with disabilities and minority communities, which are clearly stipulated by the constitution. According to the 2078 census of Nepal's population, the population of persons with disabilities is 2.2 percent, and the population of minority communities is 0.4 percent. Why were these significant populations not included in this bill? Why could this constitutional provision not be upheld? I seek an answer to this. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable member Khamm Bahadur Khatri.

Honorable Mr. Khamm Bahadur Khatri (Nepali Congress): - Honorable Chairperson,
Regarding Article 84, Sub-section (3) of the Constitution, it is stated that political parties, when nominating candidates, must ensure the representation of persons with disabilities. In this context, our Representative Council Member Election Act, 2074, has calculated representation based on percentages in the previous and current contexts, and tables have been prepared. It is stated that a provision exists for preparing a closed list in Section 28. In the Representative Council Member Election Act, 2074, Section 5 and Section 6 mention the provision for backward regions and the fact that persons with disabilities are not included in the schedule. Therefore, it appears that what needs to be added is related to Section 28, Sub-section (5), and Section 60, Sub-section (6) of Schedule 1. It seems that Section 28, Sub-section (6) should be mentioned. Furthermore, Rule 1 of the Representative Council Member Election Regulations, 2074, provides for the submission of a closed list of candidates, which is provided for in Section 28 of the Act. In Schedule 1 of Rule 14, Sub-rule (1), it is included. In the case of backward regions and persons with disabilities, although the provisions are mentioned in the constitution and the act, and also in the regulations, they are not included in the schedule of the act. Therefore, the provision in the regulations is not in the act, and the provision in the constitution is not reflected in the act. I wish to draw the attention of the Honorable Chairperson to the fact that Section 28, Sub-section (6) should be mentioned in the schedule. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable members, the discussion on the proposal for consideration of the "Bill to Amend the Representative Council Member Election Act, 2083," received with a message from the House of Representatives, concludes here. Honorable members, I now provide time to the Honorable Minister for Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Ms. Sovita Gautam, on behalf of the Honorable Prime Minister and Home Minister, Mr. Balendra Shah, to respond to the questions raised during the discussion.

Honorable Minister for Law, Justice, and Parliamentary Affairs, Ms. Sovita Gautam: -
(3:27 PM)
Honorable Chairperson, Article 84, Sub-section (2) of the Constitution of Nepal states that when political parties nominate candidates for elections under the proportional representation system, they shall ensure representation based on population, including women, Dalits, Adivasi Janajati, Khas-Arya, Madhesi, Tharu, Muslim, and from backward regions, through a closed list, as per federal law. Schedule 1 of the Representative Council Member Election Act, 2074, contains provisions regarding the percentage of inclusive groups that must be represented in the closed list. As per the report of the National Census conducted in 2078 BS, based on population, it has become necessary to determine the percentages for Dalits, Adivasi Janajati, Khas-Arya, Madhesi, Tharu, and Muslim populations. Therefore, the Representative Council Member Election First Amendment Ordinance, 2082, has been amended as per Article 114, Sub-section (1) of the Constitution of Nepal and has already been approved by this assembly. As it is necessary to maintain the provisions made by the said ordinance, the "Representative Council Member Election First Amendment Bill, 2083" has now been presented to the National Assembly for clause-by-clause discussion. I feel that the points raised by the honorable members are appropriate. No one is above the Constitution of Nepal. The Constitution of Nepal is the supreme law of our country, and if there are any matters that contradict the constitution, they must be reviewed. Regarding the issue of persons with disabilities, the previous government, the government that conducted the election, brought this ordinance before conducting the election. It was brought as an ordinance based on census data for election purposes, and we have now brought it as a replacement bill. If there are matters that need amendment, the government will take a positive view. Especially in the case of persons with disabilities, we will certainly consider it. Regarding backward regions, as raised by the honorable member, there will be time for amendments. The government will accept those matters in a way that does not contradict the constitution. I wish to say only this for now. Thank you.

Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable members, the discussion on the proposal for consideration of the "Bill to Amend the Representative Council Member Election Act, 2083," received with a message from the House of Representatives, concludes here.

Honorable members, I now present the proposal for consideration of the "Bill to Amend the Representative Council Member Election Act, 2083," received with a message from the House of Representatives, for decision.

Honorable members who are in favor of this proposal shall say "Aye" and those who are against it shall say "Nay."

Honorable members who are in favor of this proposal shall say "Aye."
- Aye

Honorable members who are against this proposal shall say "Nay."
"Nay" was not heard. The proposal for consideration of the "Bill to Amend the Representative Council Member Election Act, 2083," received with a message from the House of Representatives, has been unanimously approved.

I will make an announcement. Honorable members, I would like to inform you that honorable members wishing to submit amendment proposals to the "Electoral Roll (First Amendment) Bill, 2083" can submit their amendment proposals to the legislative branch within the National Assembly in accordance with Rule 106 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075. Honorable members, I will now provide time for the Honorable Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Sobita Gautam, on behalf of the Right Honorable Prime Minister and Home Minister, Balendra Shah, to present the proposal for consideration of the "Electoral Roll (First Amendment) Bill, 2083", received with a message from the House of Representatives. Honorable Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Ms. Sobita Gautam: (14:31 hrs) Honorable Chairperson, with the permission of the Chairperson, I present before this honorable assembly the proposal for consideration of the "Electoral Roll (First Amendment) Bill, 2083", received with a message from the House of Representatives. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the discussion on the proposal for consideration of the "Electoral Roll (First Amendment) Bill, 2083", received with a message from the House of Representatives, presented by the Right Honorable Prime Minister and Home Minister, will now commence. I would like to inform the honorable members that the discussion can only be held on the theoretical aspects of the bill and its related clauses. Honorable members who wish to participate in the discussion are requested to submit their names within two minutes. I have allocated three minutes for each honorable member participating in the discussion. Honorable Padam Bahadur Pariyar. Honorable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress):- Honorable Chairperson, we are discussing the bill to amend the "Electoral Roll Act, 2073". Specifically, this bill states that notwithstanding anything written, it shall apply in the situation where the House of Representatives is dissolved before the completion of its term and an election date is announced. This ordinance was brought in view of the situation prior to the election held on Falgun 29, 2082, and its replacement bill has now come. However, generally, such circumstances do not always occur, and if the process of registering names in the electoral roll continues even after the election date has been set, it can lead to significant questions about the credibility of the election and the election results. The government can manipulate voter registration, and ultimately, it can alter the election results. Therefore, if we include such provisions in the law, we cannot imagine a free and fair election. Thus, although we have recognized it in the specific circumstance of the Falgun 21 election in principle, I would like to inform you that it is not possible to accept it in principle. I would also like to know the opinion of the concerned ministry in this regard. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable member Suresh Kumar Ale Magar. Honorable Mr. Suresh Kumar Ale Magar (Communist Party of Nepal):- Honorable Chairperson, we are discussing the "Electoral Roll (First Amendment) Bill, 2083". I would like to reiterate that the then-election government did the right thing regarding the electoral roll. Because on the 23rd of Bhadra last year, there was an agitation. I am referring to the agitation of Bhadra 23rd, a justified agitation with justified demands. The agitation on the 24th was not an agitation; it was destruction, arson, vandalism, and criminal activity. The government formed thereafter brought certain things to conduct the election, and at that time, we had to make some amendments to the electoral roll. Because some individuals had become eligible to vote for this election. In that context, the then-government, through the ordinance, brought these two bills with the objective of completing the election, and the bill that has now come to replace that ordinance is here to replace those ordinances and give them legal form. In this sense, it is fine. The provisions for correcting the electoral roll were also minimal. I would like to state that the current government should not take such steps in the future. Another thing I would like to state is that while correcting the voter rolls is fine, we also need to consider how the subsequent election will be. We need to look at how much impact the new, updated electoral roll will have on that election, as the honorable member mentioned. Therefore, the election held in Nepal on Falgun 21st last year, with its unprecedented nature and results, has been accepted by all of us. However, I would also like to state that this should remain only an exception. Because an exception is not a general rule, and general policies should not be made based on it. In the future, sufficient time must be given for correcting voter rolls, etc. This bill has been brought in a hurry, as if we have to hold a National Assembly meeting even on holidays to complete 60 days. I hope the government will not do this in the future. I would like to request that the government pay attention to this not only in this matter but in all matters. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the discussion on the proposal for consideration of the "Electoral Roll (First Amendment) Bill, 2083", received with a message from the House of Representatives, concludes here. Honorable members, I will now provide time for the Honorable Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Sobita Gautam, on behalf of the Right Honorable Prime Minister and Home Minister, Balendra Shah, to respond to the questions raised in the discussion. Honorable Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Ms. Sobita Gautam:- (15:37 hrs) Honorable Chairperson, Section 4, Sub-section (2) of the Electoral Roll Act, 2073, states that the Election Commission may, at a time and place determined by the Commission, collect and update the electoral roll at once or in installments. It is also stipulated that after the announcement of the election date, voter registration for the purpose of that election shall not be carried out, and other arrangements, including informing the public about the collection and updating of the electoral roll, shall be made as specified. As per the Election Commission's notice dated 2082/3/16, the collection of electoral rolls was postponed, and as per the notice from the Office of the President dated 2082/5/27, the then-House of Representatives was dissolved by the Right Honorable President upon the recommendation of the Right Honorable Prime Minister, and an election for the Federal Parliament's House of Representatives was scheduled for 2082/11/21. Therefore, to collect, register, and update the electoral roll for voting in that election, Sub-section 2(a) has been added after Section 4, Sub-section (2) of the Electoral Roll Act, 2073, to provide for the Election Commission to set a period for collecting, registering, and updating the electoral roll in the event of the dissolution of the House of Representatives before the completion of its term and the announcement of an election date. This ordinance, which amended the Electoral Roll Act, 2073, in accordance with Article 114, Sub-section (1) of the Constitution of Nepal, has already been approved by this assembly. As it is necessary to maintain the provisions made by that ordinance, clause-by-clause discussion on the "Electoral Roll (First Amendment) Bill, 2083" is currently underway. Now, regarding the points raised here, it has been said that the dissolution of the House of Representatives does not happen always; it is an exception. Let us hope that these remain exceptions, and in the future, there will be no situations where the House of Representatives is dissolved before its term. Dissolutions of the House of Representatives have occurred in Nepal's history, and even after the promulgation of the current constitution, there have been dissolutions of the House of Representatives. I have used the plural "dissolutions" here, and you all understand why. Let us hope that in the future, the House of Representatives will not be dissolved before its term. However, if it happens, this provision will allow those who can participate in that election to register within the time specified by the government. If this happens, suppose an election is due in 5 years, and I plan to get my name added to the voter list by some means before that. If the House of Representatives is dissolved, then my plan will be disrupted. Consequently, that person's right to vote will be curtailed. Therefore, I believe this clause, this law, will be helpful in ensuring those things. Specifically, why is voter registration not done after the election date is announced? It is because the voter list needs to be finalized before the election. This practice is done to prevent last-minute manipulations. It is also done to verify data, such as determining the number of booths needed and the number of people who will come. This practice is followed in democratic countries to prepare for these aspects before the election date is announced. It is also a practice to avoid disputes. Therefore, I believe that the proposal made now, brought through an ordinance and proposed in the replacement bill, will help ensure the voter's right to vote, even if something goes wrong. This arrangement has kept the path open for registering on the voter list. I don't think this is a matter of much objection, and since it ensures the citizen's right, I would like to submit these points to the honorable members. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, the discussion on the proposal for consideration of the "Electoral Roll (First Amendment) Bill, 2083", received with a message from the House of Representatives, concludes here. Honorable members, I will now present the proposal for consideration of the "Electoral Roll (First Amendment) Bill, 2083", received with a message from the House of Representatives, for a decision. Honorable members in favor of this proposal will say "Aye" and honorable members against it will say "Nay". Honorable members in favor of this proposal, say "Aye". - "Aye" Honorable members against this proposal, say "Nay". The sound of "Nay" was not heard. Therefore, I declare that the proposal for consideration of the "Electoral Roll (First Amendment) Bill, 2083", received with a message from the House of Representatives, has been unanimously approved. Honorable members, I would like to inform you that honorable members wishing to submit amendment proposals to the "Electoral Roll (First Amendment) Bill, 2083" can submit their amendment proposals to the legislative branch within the National Assembly in accordance with Rule 106 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075. Honorable members, at 4:00 PM on Jestha 15, 2083, the Federal Parliament...

The Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle will present the annual estimate of revenue and expenditure for the upcoming fiscal year 2083/084 in the joint meeting of both houses, and all honorable members are requested to enter the House of Representatives meeting hall by 3:45 PM and take their seats. Honorable members, the next meeting of the National Assembly will convene on Jyestha 15, 2083, Friday, at 4:45 PM, and this meeting is hereby adjourned. Thank you. (Subsequently, this meeting was adjourned to convene on Jyestha 15, 2083, Friday, at 5:45 PM.) Adjourned: 94:44 PM.

sections.summary_en: The Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs presented the Electoral Roll (First Amendment) Bill, 2083, for consideration. Honorable members Padam Bahadur Pariyar and Suresh Kumar Ale Magar debated the bill, focusing on its implications for voter registration and election credibility, particularly in the context of past dissolutions of the House of Representatives. The Minister then responded to the concerns raised.
